toml:
# ESA Celeste IOD, signal configuration #1, all bands over one pass. WORKSHOP PRESET.
#
# This scenario uses the celeste-iod preset, whose signal parameters were presented at the
# ESA NAVISP (Navigation Innovation and Support Programme) LEO-PNT workshop, 2026, and have no
# public source yet. It can be withheld with src/leo_link/presets/celeste_iod.rs (see that
# file). Every other leo-pass scenario runs without it.
#
# A user near ESTEC in Noordwijk sees one pass of a Celeste in-orbit demonstration satellite
# (510 km sun-synchronous, public) peaking at 75 deg, on every band of the preset, next to
# Galileo E1. The preset's EIRP and beam are calibrated to the C/N0 trace shown at the workshop
# (a bell of a few minutes peaking near 57.5 dB-Hz, several dB above Galileo), so this
# scenario reproduces that trace by construction; the other bands follow from the same EIRP
# and beam at their own frequencies, with rain (20 mm/h exceeded 0.01 % of the year) and the
# first-order ionosphere on each.
#
# MODELLED (workshop-calibrated). Not a measurement of any Celeste satellite.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "Celeste IOD multi-band pass"
epoch = "2026-09-28T08:00:00"
duration_s = 600.0
step_s = 2.0
iono_free_pairs = [["E5", "C"], ["UHF", "C"], ["E5", "SR"]]

[user]
environment = "ground"
lat_deg = 52.218
lon_deg = 4.420
height_m = 5.0

[atmosphere]
rain_rate_mm_h = 20.0
rain_height_km = 2.4

[[satellite]]
id = "Celeste-IOD"
system = "celeste-iod"
max_elevation_deg = 75.0
tca_s = 300.0

[gnss]
constellation = "galileo"
band = "E1"
